subject: Sentinel AI — technical alignment & action plan
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@sentinel.ai>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@sentinel.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Sentinel AI — technical alignment & action plan

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. This note summarizes the technical fit we discussed, the top product goals you shared, and the action items we recommend so we can move from discovery to a scoped POC. Please correct anything I missed.

High-level goals you described
- Improve ranking quality for search/answer flows using embeddings + rerank.
- Enable a low-latency assistant (human-in-the-loop triage) with streaming responses and function calls into your data plane.
- Extract structured metadata from conversations (entities + categorical labels) for downstream workflows.

Primary pain points
- Current embeddings pipeline has high variance across content types and slow batch rebuilds (daily).
- Latency spike during peak hours for live assistant ( > 400ms / token worst-case ).
- Tight constraints on data residency for certain customers (contracts require customer-managed VPC).

Fit / proposed integration areas
1) Embeddings + rerank: Redwood embeddings endpoint + lightweight rerank lift using vector similarity + token-level reranking. We'll propose a small eval on ~10k ground truth pairs.
2) Streaming assistant: Redwood streaming SDK for server push; function calling for retrieval + tool execution (e.g., call your internal doc search API).
3) Structured outputs: JSON schema support to enforce consistent entity / label outputs for ingestion into your workflows.

SDK & product notes (initial):
- We will provide a streaming client (beta) that supports token-level callbacks and an optional final JSON schema validation hook.
- Function calling will follow a JSON-schema-first approach; Redwood can host a small shim for your retrieval endpoints if you prefer.
- Embeddings: support for 1024-d and 1536-d vectors depending on model; we can run a dimensionality comparison during the POC.

Immediate action items
- Sentinel: share a sample of 5–10 representative queries + expected scoring (Aisha) — due EOD Friday.
- Redwood: provide an SDK diff showing the streaming API and a short sample that wires a function call into your retrieval (Ben) — ETA Tue 10/26.
- Technical deep-dive: 60–90m session focused on streaming latency, KV cache behavior, and deployment options (canary vs dedicated). Proposed windows: Oct 27–29. Karthik to lead.

Attachments: I included a short appendix with the integration checklist; I also flagged items we need to understand better (traffic curve, PII constraints).

If that matches your read, I’ll get the SDK patch and a calendar invite for the deep-dive.

Best,
Ben

Priorities (short term)
- Rerank lift for our on-site search (primary).
- Streaming assistant latency under 200ms/token at p95 for 128-token responses (goal).

Constraints / questions
- Data residency: several enterprise customers require logs retained in our Azure tenant. Can Redwood support a private deployment (VPC/on-prem) for the POC?
- Tokenization: our current pipeline uses a proprietary tokenizer pre-processing step; what’s the recommended approach to ensure embedding parity?
- Cost estimates: ballpark delta between hosted vs dedicated for expected traffic (see traffic estimates in attachment).

I’ve attached a short deck with three example queries and our expected relevance labels (sentinel_prod_usecases.pdf). Also looping in Tom who will help surface infra constraints.

Aisha — thanks for the clear priorities and the deck. Short answers to your questions below, and a couple of notes for the deep-dive.

Data residency / deployment:
- Private deployment: yes — Redwood Private (VPC) is supported for POCs. For the POC we can provision a short-lived VPC instance in Azure (customer-managed VNet peering). We’ll need a short network checklist (firewall egress, peering CIDRs).

Tokenization / embedding parity:
- If you keep pre-tokenization, we recommend sending raw text to Redwood and letting our tokenizer run in the SDK for parity; alternatively we can accept your token ids if you expose the mapping. We’ll run a small alignment test during the POC.

Latency / streaming:
- Typical streaming SLOs we observe: 40–120ms per token at p50–p95 on Dedicated NVIDIA A10 / H100-like setups, depending on batch sizes and KV cache locality. Continuous batching helps throughput but can add 10–30ms at tail if aggressively batched.

Cost (hosted vs dedicated):
- High-level: Hosted is lower up-front but variable at scale; Dedicated gives predictable unit costs and lower p95 latency. I’ll attach a short cost comparison in the SDK diff.

Planned SDK/API changes (what we’ll deliver before deep-dive):
- streaming.generate(stream=true) client with token callback and mid-stream function_call hook.
- function_call schema: JSON-schema-first definition and a small helper to validate outputs before committing.
- structured_output param to pin a schema and receive a validated JSON object in responses.
- embeddings: both 1024 and 1536 dims; we’ll run your dataset against both and include similarity baselines.

Next steps / schedule
- Ben: push SDK diff + short cost sketch (by Tue 10/26) — done (see attachment).
- Karthik: deep-dive to focus on KV cache strategy and canary deployment options (Oct 28, 10–11:30am PT).
- Sentinel: share sample queries + traffic profile (EOD 10/23).

HubSpot: I updated the deal record and added the POC checklist link: https://hubspot.com/deals/DEAL-2026-1892

If that works I’ll send the calendar invite for Oct 28 and Karthik will share a short pre-read.

Best,
Ben
